### Phase Q0: quality/density harness, section-byte attribution and the promotion bounds for the quality track

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.quality-q0-harness-attribution/1` · part of `@jpegxl-rs.track.encoder-optimization/1`

Speed is done (Phases 30-42: Balanced 15-25% faster than cjxl -e7 at SSIMULACRA2 parity, ~13% larger files). Open the quality/density track: (1) CLI research controls --dead-zone-scale (EncodeRequest.dead_zone_scale, default 1.0 = exact nearest rule, byte-identical), --tolerance, and --sections (per-SectionKind byte breakdown from CodestreamSizing); (2) a standing harness under .agent/scratch/quality-track/ (ladder.sh: mid/large photo x 0.5/1/2 bpp x Fast/Balanced/Quality, djxl + jxl-oxide decodes, jpxl compare; cjxl-match.sh: cjxl -e7 -d bisected to matched bytes; summarise.py: deltas, BD-SSIM2/BD-rate, speed sidecar, determinism, verdict); (3) attribution of the density gap by section bytes and ablations. First finding: --sections shows LF-group sections at ~38% of a 1 bpp VarDCT stream (mid 205 of 539 KB, large 567 of 1496 KB) because write_modular_stream codes every control image with a one-leaf tree and one flat prefix code sized by the largest residual; a temporary trace measured the metadata stream (CfL, BlockInfo, Sharpness) at 44.8 KB of tokens against a 6.4 KB order-0 entropy and the LF planes at ~150 KB against ~114 KB order-0 in the larger mid LF group. That lossless recoding is Phase Q0b (jpegxl-rs.work.quality-q0b-lf-group-entropy) and is funded before Q1.

### Phase Q0b: entropy-code the LF-group control images (LF planes, CfL, BlockInfo, Sharpness) with per-channel ANS histograms and a bounded MA-tree context model

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.quality-q0b-lf-group-entropy/1` · part of `@jpegxl-rs.track.encoder-optimization/1`

Replace write_modular_stream's one-leaf tree + flat prefix code (H.2/H.4.2 minimal writer) with a real modular coder for VarDCT's control images: an MA tree whose root chain splits on the channel-index property so each channel owns its contexts, a bounded greedy learner over the static Table H.4 neighbourhood properties (|N|, |W|, west gradient error, W-NW, NW-N, N-NE, N-NN, W-WW; no property 15 so no self-correcting predictor is needed at the decoder) with a fixed threshold grid and a token-entropy price, and per-context ANS histograms with hybrid-uint configuration search (prefix codes tried where cheaper). Same decisions, same decoded pixels; fewer bytes. Under target-rate presets the rate loop hands the saved bytes to HF. Cost cap: the writer runs once per priced/stored codestream per LF group (about six times per Balanced encode), so learning is O(samples x properties) with small constants and the total Balanced wall stays inside the track's +15% budget; measured with the pinned sidecar. Gate: fixed-quantizer decode identity (pixels) through jpxl-decode, djxl and jxl-oxide; section bytes down; target-rate quality screen per Q0 bounds; 1-vs-4-thread hash equality.
